title: Judging the Past: Habría Sido Mejor Que…

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the *pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo* from B1 Unit 37, as in Es una lástima que no haya venido, and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb from B1 Unit 38. Put them together: when the main verb is in the past and the thing you are judging happened before it, the verb after *que* is *hubiera* + participle. *Fue una lástima que no hubiera venido* "It was a pity that she had not come".

sections.title: Present or past?
rows: It surprises me that she has come. (now: *haya*)
It surprised me that she had come. (then: *hubiera*)
Es una lástima que no hayan avisado.
It is a pity that they have not warned us.
Fue una lástima que no hubieran avisado.
It was a pity that they had not warned us.

sections.title: Three frames for judging the past
rows: Habría sido mejor que hubiéramos salido antes.
It would have been better if we had left earlier.
Me sorprendió que no hubieran avisado.
It surprised me that they had not warned us.
No creía que hubieran terminado tan pronto.
I did not think they had finished so soon.

sections.title: Past judgment or present advice
sections.content: The first frame judges something that was not done. For the present or the future the verb is in the imperfect subjunctive: *Sería mejor que saliéramos ahora* "It would be better if we left now". Compare it with *Habría sido mejor que hubiéramos salido antes*, which looks back.

items.spanish: Fue una lástima que no hubieras venido a la fiesta.
items.english: It was a pity that you had not come to the party.

items.spanish: Dudaba que lo hubiesen decidido tan rápido.
items.english: I doubted that they had decided it so fast.

items.spanish: Habría sido más oportuno que nos hubieran avisado antes.
items.english: It would have been more timely if they had warned us earlier.

sections.content: Use *hubiera* + participle only when the thing happened before the past verb, or before a moment you are looking back from. If the two things happen at the same time, use the imperfect subjunctive: *No creía que viniera* "I did not think he would come", but *No creía que hubiera venido* "I did not think he had come".
